app.title: Dunceious: browser genome and multiple sequence alignment workbench
app.summary: A person loads GenBank or FASTA records by picking or dropping files, then applies an alignment by uploading a pre-aligned FASTA or by sending the records to a remote alignment service. They read the alignment in a zoomable viewer where annotations follow the gaps and a conservation track is drawn. They compare every row against a chosen reference, and search for motifs with IUPAC, whole-query or local search, turning hits into annotations. They then curate annotations and sequence details in an index and export the chosen subset as FASTA, GenBank, GFF3 or a project file.

task.text: Align annotated sequences, read and compare them against a reference, search them and curate their annotations before exporting them in standard formats.

data.text: Nucleotide or protein sequence records with feature annotations and source details, optionally overlaid with a multiple alignment, plus interval or score tracks.
data.item: a sequence record with its annotated features, one row of the alignment

stage.text: exploring and annotating aligned sequences after sequencing, before downstream analysis

mechanism.text: A sidebar ingests files and drives search and alignment, while a virtualized viewer stacks every record as annotation bars over a residue track with semantic zoom, a minimap and a reference-comparison highlight. Search hits are marked in the viewer and can become annotations, which are managed in a separate Annotation Hub index that opens an export dialog with a contents preview.

field.text: multiple sequence alignment and sequence annotation in bioinformatics

workflow.name: align a set of sequences, compare them against a reference and curate their annotations

steps.here: Ingestion cards take GenBank/FASTA batches, GFF3/BED annotations or a project JSON by picking or dropping files; a session is locked to nucleotide or peptide

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Upload a pre-aligned FASTA or send the records to MAFFT, Kalign, Clustal Omega or MUSCLE; features are transposed into aligned coordinates and a consensus/conservation track is computed

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Virtualized rows stack annotation arrow bars over residues with semantic zoom from mismatch density to bases and translations, with a minimap and Pan/Select drag
Compare picks a reference row and shows Differences (identical residues as dots) or Identity, never counting ambiguity codes

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: IUPAC, whole-query (Myers, min identity) or local (Smith–Waterman, EMBOSS defaults) search on both strands; hits are marked per base and Annotate turns them into features
The Annotation Hub index groups, filters and sorts sequences and features; the feature editor changes location, strand, segments and qualifiers, with Undo for deletions
The export dialog picks a subset, a format (FASTA, GenBank/GenPept, GFF3, project) and options, and previews contents and omitted values before saving

distinctive: Feature coordinates stay ungapped while bars are transposed into alignment columns, so annotations follow the alignment without being cut at gaps.
Every computed number follows a cited reference tool (EMBOSS matcher/water, edlib, NCBI genetic codes), and metrics are defined beside their values.
Remote alignment needs explicit consent on each page load and locks edits to the record set while a job runs; aligning locally keeps all data in the browser.
Exports run through INSDC/GFF3 validation that counts every omitted qualifier or detail in a preview before the file is written.
Translation rows step at programmed ribosomal frameshifts, placing each codon in its own reading frame.
